5988.text:
5988 traṭ 'crackle', traṭiti HPariś., traṭa-traṭa - Pañcad., traṭatkāra - m. Alaṁkārat., taṭati 'rumbles' ṢaḍvBr.
[Cf. * traṭṭ-, *taḍapphaḍ -] H. taṛnā m. 'crack, report'; G. taraṛvũ intr. 'to crack,
split', taraṛ f. 'a crack'; M. taḍṇẽ intr. 'to crack, split', taḍā m. 'a fissure'; — Pa. taṭataṭāyati 'rattles, grinds
the teeth'; Pk. taḍayaḍaṁta - 'crackling', taḍataḍā - f.;
K. tar-tar m. 'crackle, fizz'; N. taṛātaṛ 'briskly'; B. Or. taṛtaṛ 'pattering, quickly'; H. taṛtaṛānā 'to burst with
a loud report'; G. taṛtaṛvũ 'to crackle', taṛtaṛ 'violently';
M. taḍāḍṇẽ 'to crack, split'; — S. ṭraṛko m. 'crackle', ṭraṛkaṇu 'to crack, split, make an uproar', P. taṛakṇā 'to
crack, crackle'; Ku. taṛak 'crackle', taṛakṇo 'to crack,
break'; N. taṛkanu 'to move briskly'; B. taṛkā 'convulsion'; H. taṛaknā 'to be cracked', taṛkā m. 'dawn'
(semant. cf. Eng. crack of dawn ); OMarw. taṛako m.
'morning'; G. taṛakvũ 'to crack', M. taḍakṇẽ ; — P. taṛākā m. 'sound of cracking wood'; B. taṛāk 'sound of
a sudden leap'; Mth. taṛāk 'suddenly'; H. taṛāk f., °kā m. 'sound of cracking'. Addenda: traṭ-: all forms in CDIAL, except S., may be <
√ taṭ .

13067 sakāla 'seasonable', °am 'early in the morning' MW.
[ sa-², kālá- ²] Paš.weg. sālāi 'awakening', chil. sōlū 'tomorrow'
IIFL iii 3, 156; Shum. sāle didaläi 'day after tomorrow';
Or. saaḷa , °ḷiā 'early', °ḷe 'promptly'.
